intro: You have reached Knidos, an ancient city in Muğla province from the 4th century BC. At the very tip of the Datça peninsula, this city of science and art had not one harbour but two.
history: Knidos was set where the Aegean meets the Mediterranean, so for ships it was an obligatory stop. But many came for something else: Praxiteles' Aphrodite drew visitors from across the ancient world.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Round Temple of Aphrodite and the Theatre, then the Sundial terrace and the Twin harbours.
facts: Did you know? The astronomer Eudoxus came from Knidos. According to ancient sources he built an observatory here and measured the year with striking accuracy, and the structure thought to be that observatory carries his name. Praxiteles' Aphrodite of Knidos was the first monumental female nude in Greek art; people sailed here simply to see it. The city had two harbours, one of them naval. Built on the cape where two seas meet, it was where ships waited out the wind.
outro: This brings our tour of Knidos to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for your company, and enjoy your visit.
